concept_html:
OneLake security controls who reads which data in OneLake: tables, folders, schemas, rows and columns. Every supported engine enforces it (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026).

Roles. Each role has a permission (Read or ReadWrite), the data it covers, and its members: Entra users or groups. The model is deny by default and supports only grant roles. There are no deny roles. A lakehouse starts with a DefaultReader role that gives users with the ReadAll permission access to its data. Remove or narrow it before your own roles mean anything.

Who it restricts. OneLake security governs Viewers and users with Read permission on the item. Workspace Admins, Members and Contributors already have data access through their workspace role. Make analysts Viewers.

Row and column security. A role can filter rows (RLS) and hide columns (CLS) on a table. Within one role, access is the intersection of its table, row and column rules. Across roles, access is the union: row filters combine with OR, so a user in roles for city = 'Leeds' and city = 'York' sees both cities. Two exceptions:

  • In the SQL analytics endpoint, CLS uses deny semantics: if any of the user's roles hides a column, the endpoint blocks it.
  • SELECT * on a table with hidden columns returns the allowed columns in Spark, but fails in the SQL analytics endpoint.

Keep row and column rules that belong together in the same role. OneLake rejects a combination where two roles allow different columns of a table and either role also filters its rows. Roles with ReadWrite cannot carry RLS or CLS.

Engines. RLS and CLS are GA in Spark notebooks, lakehouses, Direct Lake on OneLake semantic models, and the SQL analytics endpoint in user's identity access mode. Eventhouse supports RLS only, in preview.

`Literal` from `typing` limits a parameter to fixed values: `mode: Literal["fast", "safe"]` tells readers and mypy that only those two strings are valid. Python does not check it at run time, so a caller can still pass any string. Raise an error yourself when a wrong value must not get through.

`set().union(*sets)` combines sets: every item in any of them. `set.intersection(*sets)` keeps only items in all of them.

solution_lines: from typing import Literal
def visible_columns(
roles: list[dict[str, set[str]]],
table: str,
engine: Literal["spark", "sql_endpoint"],
) -> set[str]:
"""Columns a user sees in one table across their OneLake security roles.
Args:
roles: Each role maps table names to the columns it allows.
table: Table being queried.
engine: "spark" (union across roles) or "sql_endpoint" (intersection).
Returns:
Visible column names. Empty if no role includes the table.
Raises:
ValueError: If the engine is not recognised.
"""
if engine not in ("spark", "sql_endpoint"):
raise ValueError(f"unknown engine: {engine}")
grants = [role[table] for role in roles if table in role]
if not grants:
return set()
if engine == "spark":
return set().union(*grants)
return set.intersection(*grants)

title: OneLake security, roles down to rows and columns
why_html: A team added a OneLake security role limiting analysts to UK rows of fact_sales, then found the analysts still saw every country. Two causes. The analysts were Contributors on the workspace, so roles did not restrict them. And the DefaultReader role was still in place, granting full reads to every Viewer with ReadAll. Making analysts Viewers and removing DefaultReader fixed both.
